 Prince Harry’s friend reveals how the Duke really feels about King Charles' Sandringham Christmas snub
 A friend of Prince Harry has revealed how he really feels after failing to secure an invite to the Royal Family's Christmas celebration a Sandringham. 
 Megan Watts Lifestyle Reporter 2 min read November 16, 2026 - 12:30PM Prince Harry feels "comfortable" not spending Christmas at Sandringham with the Royal Family, a loyal friend claims. 
 It has been widely reported that the 42-year-old Duke of Sussex, along with his wife Meghan Markle, 45, and children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, will be spending the Christmas holidays in the United Kingdom.
 However, sources confirmed to the Daily Mail Harry's brood had not been invited to the Royal Family's annual celebration at the King's Sandringham Estate in Norfolk.
 Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, delivers a speech during the Kyiv Security Forum on April 23, 2026 in Kyiv, Ukraine. Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, founder of the Invictus Games Foundation, arrives in Ukraine and takes part in the 18th Kyiv Security Forum. Picture: Andrii Khodkov/Apostrophe/Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images According to the publication, sources pointed to some people having "strong feelings" as the reason for the snub, alluding to the reported rift between Harry and his brother Prince William, 44.
 However, Sussex insiders have denied an estrangement.
 Now, a friend of the Duke has told the Daily Mail Harry is "relaxed" about not being invited to spend Christmas with his royal relatives and is, instead, looking on the bright side. 
 "Harry says that he is really looking forward to a cold Christmas," they shared, adding that he is "really comfortable that he is not required to be in Sandringham".
 "He’s comfortable that he can spend time with his family."
 The friend went on to note "they are all so busy" but expects Harry will see his father before Christmas on a "private basis". 
 "He’s really comfortable with that – he’s had his hands full. He came back in the third week of August and his diary has been very full from that point."
 The publication claims the family intended on going back to California for the holidays, but the children are "doing so well" adjusting to their new life in the UK and are looking forward to a British Christmas.
 The family are understood to be "making early plans" to celebrate Christmas in the Cotswolds. Picture: Supplied The family are understood to be "making early plans" to celebrate Christmas in the Cotswolds and will be joined by Meghan's mum Doria Ragland, 70, according to Hello.
 The Sussexes returned to the United Kingdom in August after living in the United States for six years.
 Prince Harry revealed in an interview with GQ Magazine last month one of the main reasons they decided to relocate was "opportunities for the family".

 He also noted "being closer to family" as a major factor that influenced their move. 
 However, it is understood that Prince Harry is yet to have a private meeting with his father King Charles, 77, despite relocating to Britain three months ago.
